author: sbutnari
title: GPU unit tests fail to extract OpenVINO package - PowerShell execution policy disabled scripts on Windows runner
signature: cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: "Extract OpenVINO packages" step fails because the self-hosted runner's PowerShell is configured with a Restricted execution policy, so the generated PS1 wrapper for Expand-Archive cannot be loaded.

key_errors: File C:\actions-runner\_work\_temp\f43cb258-40cc-4e0b-9fb9-9dbdc960e6c1.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system. For more information, see about_Execution_Policies at https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=135170.
root_cause: The job's 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs 'Expand-Archive ... -Force' via a GitHub Actions-generated temporary .ps1 wrapper script. On the self-hosted Windows GPU runner that executed this job, the PowerShell execution policy is set to Restricted (or similarly locked down) at the machine/user scope, so Windows PowerShell refuses to load any .ps1 file and raises PSSecurityException/UnauthorizedAccess. This is unrelated to the PR's source changes (NPU blob importer code) and is a runner environment misconfiguration - either the runner was freshly provisioned/reimaged without the expected 'RemoteSigned'/'Bypass' execution policy, or a GPO/local policy reset it. The step fails deterministically on this specific runner regardless of what script content is generated.
reproduction_steps: On the same (or an identically configured) self-hosted Windows runner, open PowerShell and run 'Get-ExecutionPolicy -List'. If any scope resolves to 'Restricted' ahead of 'RemoteSigned'/'Unrestricted'/'Bypass', then running any .ps1 (e.g., a trivial 'Expand-Archive' wrapper) will reproduce the PSSecurityException seen in the job log. Not reproducible via a code change in the PR; this is runner-environment-specific and not reproducible purely from source.
recommended_actions: Set the PowerShell execution policy to RemoteSigned (or Bypass for CI) at the LocalMachine scope on the affected runner via 'Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine -Force' (or equivalent GPO fix), then verify with 'Get-ExecutionPolicy -List'.
Re-run the failed 'GPU unit tests' job; GitHub Actions self-hosted runner pools often route to a different machine on retry, which may already have a correct policy.
Add a runner health check / startup script that asserts 'Get-ExecutionPolicy' is not 'Restricted' before accepting jobs, to fail fast with a clearer error instead of a late pipeline failure.
Audit the intel-gpu Windows self-hosted runner pool for other machines with the same misconfiguration to prevent recurrence.
prevention_strategies: Add runner provisioning automation (or a scheduled compliance check) that enforces 'Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine' as part of the Windows self-hosted runner image/bootstrap, and alert if a runner drifts from this baseline before it picks up CI jobs.
historical_context: Repo-memory contains a related but distinct pattern (95bb23aa2ed8a84d, count 12) for the same step/job ('GPU unit tests' Extract OpenVINO packages) failing with 'UnauthorizedAccessException' due to a locked tbb12.dll file. That is a file-lock issue, not an execution-policy issue - different root cause, so a separate pattern record is used. No prior occurrence of the execution-policy variant was found in the knowledge base; this is the first recorded instance (count 1).
